requirements.expectation: Mock-admission loopback bootstrap: the fixture ensures the local Human principal endpoint answers and reads a one-time registration token before any business request; every later call carries the Human mock identity headers.

The story registers the disposable Policy-story-driver Bot with the one-time token and onboards it with testing domain, review skill and local scope; the lifetime is provider-free with no scripted Provider or Judge mock.

Both legacy service_spec encodings (a disabled policy object and a null compatibility shim) stay accepted at group creation while persisting nothing: the created group, the read-back group and every response payload are free of service_spec and retired_service_spec.
Patching group settings with a legacy service_spec is rejected as Gone with status 410 and the exact service_policy_retired error; the retirement is observable instead of silently ignored.

Neither the retired disabled flag nor max_concurrency=1 gates service invocation: two distinct service_invocation Sessions return 202 running with session_kind service_invocation, each persists its submitted input, and the two invocations never share a Session id.
Retirement does not allow reactivating a running invocation: posting the session_id of a running invocation is refused with 409 and a running-shaped error while the stored input stays unmodified.

A completed chat Session cannot be converted into a service invocation (400 with a not-service_invocation error), and the completed chat Session keeps its completed status and output intact after the refused conversion.
Teardown deletes every Session with the bot_id query, both Groups with the bot_id query and the disposable Bot; any cleanup failure fails the whole story instead of leaking state.
